subject: Emotions
title: Purity Laws and Religion
description: Learn Purity Laws and Religion in one minute.

hook.text: Kosher and halal rules aren't just about faith. They're ancient food safety encoded as religious law.

buildup.text: Every major religion has purity codes. Hinduism, Judaism, Islam, and Shinto all define clean and unclean.

discovery.text: Mary Douglas argued purity rules create social order. What's 'dirty' is whatever crosses a boundary.

twist.text: Pork bans may trace to trichinosis risk. Religious law preserved survival knowledge as sacred command.

climax.text: Purity rituals persist because they bind communities. Shared disgust creates group identity.

punchline.text: Every religion has a list of things you should find gross.

quiz.question: What did Mary Douglas argue about purity rules?
